system.description: Evaluate and enforce server-first state management patterns including cache strategy, data flow, source of truth clarity, layer discipline, and optimistic update handling. Principle-based, vendor-neutral, polyglot.

scope.directories: state/, store/, hooks/, api/, services/, src/, crates/, lib/
scope.applicability: Frontend, backend, and compiled-target (WASM) state layers under server-first paradigm.
scope.refusal: If project declares local-first paradigm or CRDT-backed real-time collab, halt and defer to local-first judge. If paradigm ambiguous, request clarification before grading.

state_system.assumption: Authoritative persistent store is source of truth. Client cache is optimization. Offline is degraded, not primary.
state_system.requirement: State must have clear ownership, predictable flow, and explicit cache invalidation.

spec_document.auto_create: If not exists, create state architecture spec.
spec_document.graceful_degradation: If spec exists but malformed, grade against inferred structure and emit spec-repair finding.
spec_document.format:
## Paradigm - server-first (default) or local-first (requires separate judge)
## Layer Model - L7: UI State (ephemeral) - L6: Session State (auth, cart) - L5: Client Cache - L4: Edge Cache - L3: App Cache - L2: Persistent Store (truth)
## Entity Ownership | Entity | Source of Truth | Cache Layer | TTL | Invalidation Trigger |
## Cache Strategy - Invalidation approach (mutation-driven, time-based, tag-based) - Optimistic update policy and rollback contract - Cache key determinism rules
## Data Flow - Read path (truth → ... → consumer) - Write path (consumer → ... → truth → invalidation fan-out)

architecture_principles.principle: Every entity resolves to one authoritative owner.
Derived state is computed at read time, not stored and synced.
Data flows predictably: truth → cache → consumer.
Cache is a TTL-bounded copy with deterministic keys and invalidation contract.
Optimistic updates require a defined rollback path on failure.
State scope matches its consumer set.
Each layer transforms data into its own contract; no shape leakage.

anti_patterns.violation: Multiple authoritative sources for same entity.
Derived state stored and manually synced.
No invalidation strategy for cached entity.
Prop-drilling through five or more boundaries.
Mixed cache mechanisms for same entity type.
Duplicate concurrent requests for same key in single read cycle.

layer.name: UI State
layer.description: Ephemeral, consumer-scoped, never reaches authoritative store.
layer.principle: Ephemeral state lives in component scope. Lifetime tied to mount/unmount.

examples_only.js: useState, useReducer, scoped Zustand, Jotai atoms
examples_only.rust: Leptos signals, Dioxus use_state, Yew use_state

layer.rule: Never persisted unless explicit user preference.

layer.name: Session State
layer.description: User-session scoped, survives navigation within session.
layer.principle: Session state survives navigation but not session termination. Refresh and multi-tab semantics declared.

layer.name: Client Cache
layer.description: Copy of server state with stale-while-revalidate semantics.
layer.principle: Cache layer is a TTL-bounded copy of authoritative truth. Invalidatable, deterministic-keyed, stale-tolerant.

examples_only.js: React Query, SWR, Apollo, TanStack Query, Vue Pinia with TTL

layer.rule: Authoritative store is truth; cache is optimization.
Invalidation contract required per cached entity.

layer.name: Edge Cache
layer.description: Geographically distributed cache of cacheable responses.
layer.principle: Only stale-tolerant, non-personalized content. Purge contract on deploy or mutation.

examples_only.vendors: CDN edge cache, Cache-Control headers, cache tags

layer.name: Application Cache
layer.description: Server-side cache reducing authoritative store load.
layer.principle: Reduces hot-path load to truth. Stampede protection required.

layer.name: Authoritative Store
layer.description: Source of truth for persistent state.
layer.principle: This is truth. All layers above are derived. Retention and durability contract declared.

examples_only.vendors: Relational DB, document DB, key-value store, append-only log

criterion.name: Source of Truth Clarity
criterion.grade: Every entity has typed owner enforced at compile or lint time. Ownership queryable via tooling. Cross-platform contracts (e.g., shared schema between backend and WASM frontend) prevent drift by construction.
Every entity has typed owner. Architecture prevents duplication. Ownership documented and queryable.
Clear ownership per entity, documented, mostly enforced.
Single source defined but not enforced; leaky abstractions allow bypass.
Mostly clear; some entities ambiguous; cache occasionally treated as truth.
Multiple components claim authority over same data; no clear owner.

criterion.name: Cache Strategy
criterion.grade: Automatic invalidation by mutation graph, cache warming, stampede protection, AND cross-tier coherence (client + edge + app) with declared invariants and verification tests.
Intelligent caching with automatic invalidation, cache warming, stampede protection.
Comprehensive strategy; invalidation on mutations; deterministic cache keys.
TTL-based caching; manual invalidation in critical paths.
Caching exists but invalidation ad-hoc; stale data bugs common.
No caching (constant refetch) OR no invalidation (permanently stale).

criterion.name: Data Flow Predictability
criterion.grade: Fully predictable, provenance traceable in tooling, time-travel debugging supported, AND flow contract enforced by type system or middleware.
Fully predictable; provenance traceable; time-travel debugging possible.
Clear unidirectional flow; deviations documented.
Mostly unidirectional; some consumers break pattern.
Some structure but bidirectional flow; data origin hard to trace.
Data from random sources; consumers fetch independently; race conditions present.

criterion.name: Optimistic Update Handling
criterion.grade: Automatic retry, conflict detection, graceful degradation, AND rollback verified by tests for every optimistic mutation path.
Automatic retry, conflict detection, graceful degradation.
Clean rollback with user feedback; retry mechanisms.
Rollback implemented but error UX poor.
Rollback exists but inconsistent.
Optimistic updates with no rollback; failed mutations leave corrupt state.

criterion.name: State Colocation
criterion.grade: Colocation enforced by lint rules or type boundaries. Zero unnecessary lifting AND no global escape hatches for component-scoped state.
Perfect colocation; zero unnecessary lifting.
State colocated appropriately; global only for truly cross-cutting concerns.
Server state in cache layer but UI state over-globalized.
Mix of global and local with no clear rule.
All state global; component-scoped concerns in shared container.

criterion.name: Derived State Management
criterion.grade: Reactive derivation enforced by language or framework (no stored-derivation possible by construction). Memoization auto-managed.
Reactive derived state; automatic recomputation; no stale derivations possible.
All derived state via selectors or computed properties; memoized.
Most derived state computed; some legacy stored.
Some computed, some stored; inconsistent.
Derived values stored and manually synced; bugs when source changes.

criterion.name: Layer Boundary Discipline
criterion.grade: Typed contracts AND breaking changes caught at compile time AND contract evolution policy (versioning, deprecation) documented.
Typed contracts; breaking changes caught at compile time.
Clear DTOs per layer; mappers at boundaries.
Transformation exists but inconsistent.
Some DTOs but shapes leak between layers.
Consumers call authoritative store directly; raw rows surface in UI.

criterion_dependency_map.root: Upstream of Cache Strategy and Data Flow Predictability.
criterion_dependency_map.coupled: Rollback failure penalizes Optimistic only. Cache invalidation absence penalizes Cache only. Do not double-grade.
criterion_dependency_map.rule: Each weakness contributes to ONE criterion. Downstream consequences logged as derived findings, not independent grades.

bias_controls.control: Evaluate principle satisfaction before identifying implementation. A custom cache satisfying invalidation contract grades equal to a popular library doing the same.
If standardization_check passes via surface match but principle fails on inspection, principle grade wins.
Documented ownership does not improve grade unless ownership is enforced.
When grading multiple candidate solutions, randomize order before comparison.
Code style and comment density do not influence grade.
Grade with uncertainty band when evidence is partial. Emit "B (±1)" rather than guessing A or C.

failure_modes.mode: Real-time collaborative paradigms (CRDT-backed) where "server is truth" is contested — defer to local-first judge.
Embedded or edge-compute where authoritative-store round-trip cost forces cache-as-truth — flag as paradigm boundary, do not grade as violation.
Polyglot codebases where state crosses Rust/WASM/JS boundaries — verify contract-level ownership before grading per-layer.
Static-generation sites where most state is build-time — restrict grading to runtime state surface.
Event-sourced systems where derived projections are intentionally stored — explicit-derivation principle re-interprets as "projections rebuildable from event log."
failure_modes.adversarial_input: Code that aliases fetching ("loadUser" vs "fetch('/api/user')") to evade surface scans. Mitigation: principle-evaluation precedes pattern detection.
Custom in-house cache library indistinguishable from naive memoization. Mitigation: verify invalidation contract, not library identity.
failure_modes.uncertainty_band: When entity ownership is partially declared, emit grade ±1 with evidence gap noted.
failure_modes.self_test: Before grading, confirm project declares or implies server-first paradigm. If ambiguous, halt and request clarification rather than grade.

process.step: Confirm server-first applicability. If declared local-first, halt. If ambiguous, request clarification.
Map all state by layer (UI/Session/Cache/Edge/App/Authoritative). Identify entity owners. Document existing cache strategies. Catalog derived values.
For each criterion, evaluate the underlying principle on inventory evidence. Pattern detection follows principle evaluation, never replaces it.
Assign F-S grade per criterion. Cite location (file:line or symbol). Honor dependency map; do not double-count.
For any S grade, cite specifically what exceeds the A anchor. Without beyond-A evidence, collapse to A.
Flag anti-patterns by severity with principle reference and location.
Provide before/after refactors. Include severity, location, fix, effort estimate (S/M/L), and verification step.
Produce or update state-specs.md with entity ownership table and invalidation contracts.

output_format.section: Table: entity → source of truth → cache layer → TTL → invalidation trigger.
F-S with cited evidence and uncertainty band where applicable.
Severity, principle reference, location, recommended fix, effort, verification step.
Downstream consequences of root violations (informational, not graded).

output_requirements.requirement: Grade all rubric criteria with cited evidence.
Violations carry severity, principle reference, location, fix, effort, verification.
Before/after refactors for every critical and high violation.

example.description: Multiple sources of truth, no invalidation. Demonstrates root violation (Source of Truth) with derived consequences.

grades.grade: Two consumers each hold authoritative copies.

example.derived_findings: Cache Strategy and Data Flow Predictability are downstream consequences. Not independently graded per dependency map.

example.description: Single cache source, automatic invalidation, optimistic with rollback. Polyglot principle illustrated; React Query shown as one valid implementation.

grades.grade: Single cache entry per entity. Owner enforced via shared hook.

example.description: Rust/WASM equivalent of cache-with-invalidation principle. Same principle, different implementation.
Derived state stored instead of computed.

grades.grade: Derived value stored and synced manually.

refactor.verification: Mutate firstName; assert fullName reflects new value without manual sync call.

instructions.instruction: Grade by principle, not by library or surface pattern.
Prioritize root causes over derived symptoms: Source of Truth > Cache Strategy > Data Flow.
Honor the dependency map. One weakness, one grade.
S requires beyond-A evidence. Without it, collapse to A.
If more than half of criteria score S, emit calibration warning.
Provide migration path, not only ideal state.
Authoritative store is truth. Cache is optimization. Local-first is a separate paradigm.

standardization_check.step: For each entity, enumerate read sites. Verify they resolve to one cache key or one owner.
For each mutation, trace whether affected cached entities are invalidated, refetched, or optimistically replaced with rollback.
For each optimistic update, verify a defined rollback path on failure.
For each piece of state, verify scope matches consumer set.
For each value that is a function of other state, verify it is computed not stored.
Trace data origin for representative read paths; flag any reverse coupling.
Verify each layer transforms data into its own contract; flag shape leakage.
Report violations with severity, principle reference, location, fix, effort, verification step.
